full_judgment:
4. The case of the plaintiff, in short, was that the lands of R.S. Khatian No. 2243 originally belonged to Sayed Ahmed, Bacha Miah and Anu Miah. Anu Miah sold out his entire share to Kalu Miah @ Kala Miah by registered kabala dated 24.02.1948. Kalu Miah @ Kala Miah subsequently sold out his purchased land to Mir Kashem Chowdhury the son of Bacha Miah and the defendant Nos. 4 to 6 the sons of Sayed Ahmed by registered kabala dated 04.12.1957. Bacha Miah died leaving two sons Alamgir Chowdhury and Mir Kashem Chowdhury. Sayed Ahmed died leaving sons-the defendant Nos. 4 to 6. Subsequently Mir Kashem Chowdhury also died leaving sons the defendant Nos. 7 to 11. Thus the defendant Nos. 4 to 11 acquired total 93 decimals of land in the suit khatian. That the plaintiff purchased 41 decimals of land from this defendant Nos. 4 to 11 by registered kabala dated 12.07.1988. The plaintiff executed a kabuliyat dated 04.09.1988 also in favour of his full brother Mir Kashem in respect of the suit land. That the defendants have got no right, title and possession in the suit land. The defendant Nos. to 3 filed Other Class Suit No. 85 of 1988 for permanent injunction in the court of Assistant Judge, Patiya against the defendant Nos. 4 to 11 the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiff. That suit was subsequently transferred to the court of Additional Assistant Judge, Patiya and was renumbered as Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1990. The defendant Nos. 4 to 11 contested in that suit. The plaintiff filed an application in that suit for being added as defendant but that application was rejected. That suit was ultimately decreed. The predecessors of the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No. 403 of 1990 against the judgment passed in O.C. Suit No. 52 of 1990, but that appeal was dismissed. That the plaintiff prayed for being added as party in that appeal also but that prayer also was rejected. That the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on the strength of that judgment and decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1990 and in Other Appeal No. 403 of 1990 denied the plaintiff's title in the suit land and thus the plaintiff was compelled to file the suit. 

 5. The defendant Nos.1 to 3 contested the suit by filing a written statement. Their case, in short, was that Anu Miah got the land of suit plot No. 8054 in his exclusive share by amicable settlement with his other co-sharers and at the death of Anu Miah the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 got this land by virtue of inheritance. These defendants have been possessing this land and the B.S. record also has been duly prepared in their names. That the predecessor of the plaintiff filed an objection case against that B.S. khatian but that was rejected. That the defendant Nos. 4 to 11 threatened these contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 with dispossession and as such these defendants filed Other Class Suit No. 85 of 1988 which was subsequently renumbered as Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1990 and that suit was decreed on contest and the judgment and decree of the trial court was affirmed by the appellate court also. That the said decree is binding upon the plaintiff. 

 7. Against the judgment and decree of the trial court the plaintiff preferred Other Appeal No. 467 of 2003 before the learned District Judge, Chittagong which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge and Bankruptcy Court, Chittagong. The appellate court allowed the appeal, set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and decreed the suit of the plaintiff declaring the plaintiff's title in the suit land and further declaring that the judgment and decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1990 was illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff and also declaring that the B.S. khatian of the suit land in the names of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 was wrong. 

 13. Admittedly the suit land along with other lands of R.S. khatian No. 2243 originally belonged to Syed Ahmad, Bacha Miah and Anu Miah. The plaintiffs case is that Ann Miah sold his share to Kalu Miah @ Kala Miah by registered kabala dated 24.04.1948 and Kalu Miah subsequently sold this land to Mir Kashem Chowdhury the son of Bacha Miah and the defendant Nos. 4 to 6 the sons of Sayed Ahmed. Later on Mir Kashem Chowdhury died leaving defendant Nos. 7 to 11 as his sons. The plaintiff has claimed the suit land by virtue of purchase from these defendants Nos. 4 to 11 by kabalas of the year 1988. The contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are sons of Anu Miah. These defendants denied the claim of the plaintiff and pleaded, inter-alia, that Anu Miah never sold his share to Kalu Miah @ Kala Miah and that at the death of Anu Miah they inherited the suit land and they have also been possessing the same. These contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have pleaded further that since the defendant Nos.4 to 11 threatened them with dispossession from the suit land they filed Other Class Suit No. 85 of 1988 in the 1st court of Assistant Judge, Patiya for permanent injunction against the defendant Nos. 4 to 11 and that suit was subsequently transferred to the court of Additional Assistant Judge, Patiya and was renumbered as O.C. Suit No. 52 of 1990. The defendant Nos. 4 to 11 contested in that suit and that suit was decreed by the trial court and that judgment and decree of the trial court was upheld by the appellate court in Other Appeal No. 403 of 1990. These contesting defendants have alleged that the plaintiff in collusion with their predecessors created kabala deeds in respect of the suit land during pendency of that suit most fraudulently and illegally and that the plaintiff could not acquire any right, title or possession in the suit land by virtue of his alleged purchase from the defendant Nos. 4-11
